statement: Only verifying a request's token may count it as not revoked while the revocation store cannot be read (the reader throws RevocationUnavailableException; CoSec's own reader does so for each read that does not end within 30 % of the authentication timeout (`PIP-33`), so that twice it is less than the authentication timeout for every `cosec.pipeline.timeout` of 20 ms or more, and an application's reader that never answers is cut at the authentication timeout and is a 503: the documented exception to failing closed, which whoever builds a TokenAuthenticator states, since acceptUnavailableRevocations is a required parameter with no default, and which the starter states from cosec.authentication.revocation.fail-closed: accepted unless it is set); a reader never answers "not revoked" for a read that failed, and any other error the revocation check reports fails the request with 503, never accepts the token.
guards: runtime:RevocationHangPipelineTest#a custom reader that never answers is a 503 at the authentication timeout, whatever fail-closed says
cocache:CoCacheRevocationReaderBudgetTest#a token read Redis never answers is unavailable once the budget is spent, and the shared lookup stays open
cocache:CoCacheRevocationReaderBudgetTest#a subject read Redis never answers is unavailable once the budget is spent
spring-boot:RevocationReadBudgetTest#a hanging Redis accepts the token within the reader's budget
spring-boot:RevocationReadBudgetTest#with fail-closed a hanging Redis fails the check within the reader's budget
runtime:StageBudgetsTest#a token's two revocation reads end inside the authentication budget
spring-boot:RevocationFailClosedWiringTest#by default a token is accepted while its revocations cannot be read - PIP-7
spring-boot:RevocationFailClosedWiringTest#with fail-closed a token is refused while its revocations cannot be read - PIP-7
architecture:SafeDefaultsTest#no public parameter that reads revocations or memberships has a default
architecture:SafeDefaultsTest#the scan reads the token API
